No bug that would make the result meaningless. The head's input size presumably comes from widths['block3'], and the run finished with no integrity flags, so the shapes must line up.

Recomputed z: the gain is -0.1062 - (-0.1126) = 0.0064. The noise sd of a difference between two jobs is 0.026*sqrt(2) = 0.0368, so z = 0.0064 / 0.0368 = 0.17, which matches the harness's 0.175. The gain is far inside the noise, so rejecting provisionally is reasonable.

Only one run on each side, so the evidence is weak. A narrower block3 should mainly cut time and cost some accuracy. A replicate is only worth a slot if the time-versus-accuracy split looks promising.
